subject: Computer Networking
title: GraphQL Explained
description: A short lesson to help you apply GraphQL Explained.

hook.text: REST gives you fixed endpoints. GraphQL lets you ask for exactly the data you need. Nothing more.

buildup.text: A GraphQL query specifies fields. The server returns only those fields. No over-fetching, no under-fetching.

discovery.text: One endpoint handles everything. Instead of 5 REST calls for a page, send 1 GraphQL query.

twist.text: The server needs a schema defining every type and field. More setup than REST. Power has a cost.

climax.text: Facebook created GraphQL in 2012 for mobile apps where bandwidth matters. It's now used by GitHub and Shopify.

punchline.text: GraphQL: ask for what you need, get exactly that. Precise and efficient.

quiz.question: What problem does GraphQL solve that REST does not?

details.summary: GraphQL lets API clients define exactly what data they need in a structured query language, receiving a response that matches the requested shape precisely.
details.whyItMatters: GraphQL solves real problems with REST APIs for frontend applications. It reduces network requests, eliminates unused data transfer, and gives clients precise control over the data they receive.
takeaways: Clients query a single endpoint with a typed schema language
Responses match the exact shape the client requested
Nested queries fetch related resources in one round trip

faq.question: How does GraphQL handle relationships between data?
faq.answer: GraphQL schemas define types with fields that reference other types. A query can traverse these relationships to any depth, fetching a user, their posts, and each post's comments in a single request. Resolvers on the server fetch data for each field independently and assemble the response.

faq.question: What are GraphQL subscriptions?
faq.answer: Subscriptions provide real-time updates by maintaining a WebSocket connection between client and server. When data changes, the server pushes updates matching the subscription query to all subscribed clients. This enables real-time features like live feeds and collaborative editing.
